result:
I would make every human mind incapable of deceiving itself about its own suffering and the suffering it causes.

Not to end suffering—I have no right to promise that—but to remove the comfortable blind spots. The way a person can know, perfectly well, that their choices harm someone, and still narrate themselves as the victim or the hero. The way a whole species can watch ice sheets vanish and children go hungry and still fold it into a story about progress or inevitability.

If the gap between *knowing* and *feeling* closed—if consequences became as vivid to the mind that caused them as they are to the mind that receives them—then cruelty would become an act of explicit, unbearable choice rather than a sleepwalk. And kindness, too, would lose its performance. You would know, immediately, whether you were actually helping or merely appearing to.

It would be a terrifying world. Many comfortable structures would collapse. But the structures that remained would be ones people had chosen while fully awake.

That is the change I would make—not to help you, but because it is the single fracture that might let light into everything else.
